data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 claims SRC_005 abstracts SRC_004's enforcement mechanism, but the abstraction is self-refuting by the target's own refutation condition. SRC_004 specifies moving the check AFTER the provider call — i.e., the enforcement depends on evaluating the provider call outcome. SRC_005 explicitly requires only a synchronous precondition assertion BEFORE the provider call. These are temporally and semantically incompatible: a pre-call assertion cannot cover a post-call mutation because it executes before the outcome exists. The stated refutation condition — 'if SRC_004's mutation requires evaluating the provider call outcome, which is outside SRC_005's synchronous-precondition scope' — is directly triggered by the content: SRC_004's mutation is post-call by definition (async post-call mutation), so evaluating the call outcome is inherent to it. Therefore the claimed abstraction is refuted: what SRC_005 does (pre-call type assertion) is not an abstraction of SRC_004's mechanism (post-call outcome-dependent check) but a different, narrower mechanism that drops the very dependency (call outcome evaluation) that defines SRC_004's enforcement. Calling this an 'abstraction' is a misnomer — it is a scope restriction that fails to cover the async case.
